admit site vm of f2a9c4e1-0b7d-4c3a-9e2f-5a6b7c8d9e01 as paisans-f2a9 on fake (ubuntu 24.04)

step 1: claim the host
step 2: create /etc/paisans
step 3: record what admit installs
step 4: skip the mesh until its conf exists
step 5: start paisans-f2a9's manager after the mesh
step 6: delegate cgroups to users
step 7: write the egress table
step 8: install the egress unit
step 9: load the egress table

step 10: load br_netfilter
  daemon: load br_netfilter now, which the user's daemon needs with its userland proxy off
  run:
    $ modprobe br_netfilter

step 11: load br_netfilter at boot
  daemon: list br_netfilter and nf_tables in /etc/modules-load.d/paisans.conf, shared by every admitted deployment
  write /etc/modules-load.d/paisans.conf mode 0644:
    | # Written by paisans site admit. The rootless Docker daemons of admitted
    | # deployments need br_netfilter to start with their userland proxy off,
    | # and the module their iptables uses for the setup tool to install them.
    | br_netfilter
    | nf_tables

step 12: write paisans-f2a9's daemon.json
step 13: install paisans-f2a9's rootless Docker
step 14: create /srv/paisans
step 15: create /srv/paisans/f2a9
step 16: create /etc/wireguard
step 17: create /usr/local/libexec/paisans
step 18: install the WireGuard helper
step 19: install the helper's sudoers line
step 20: allow 22/tcp
step 21: allow 51820/udp
step 22: allow all inbound on psns-f2a9

step 23: write the admission record
  record: who the deployment runs as and what you granted, which its own commands read

  Its manager is running, and restarting it would restart its Docker daemon and every container in it, so admit does not. cpuset and io limits apply after the host's next reboot.
